structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin's rule holds, no non-volant terrestrial mammal species has a present natural range that lies on an island more than ~483 km (300 statute miles) from any continent or great continental island.
structured_output.pass_criterion: After excluding Chiroptera, marine, freshwater and domesticated taxa, the count of species whose present natural range includes at least one land cell with its centroid more than 483 km from the nearest continental landmass or great continental island is 0 (zero species survive manual verification against the literature as truly native and not human-introduced).
structured_output.fail_criterion: One or more non-volant terrestrial mammal species (for example, Galápagos oryzomyine rodents, Nesoryzomys) remain after the same filters and manual verification of native status, which means a single doubt-free instance exists and the rule is refuted as stated.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Terrestrial mammal' means a non-volant, non-marine, non-freshwater species; bats are excluded because Darwin treated them as the exception that can cross sea. 'Native' means the PHYLACINE 'present natural range', which models ranges without human-caused introductions. It also includes species extinct in the last ~130,000 years, so it tests the rule against the recently extinct fauna, an extension Darwin could not have known. 'Continent or great continental island' is fixed in advance as the Americas, Afro-Eurasia, Australia and Antarctica, plus islands of at least 200,000 km² on continental shelves (New Guinea, Borneo, Madagascar, Sumatra, Honshu, Great Britain, Greenland and similar). 300 miles is taken as 483 km. Distance is computed from the 1-degree range-map cells to the nearest such landmass using a standard land polygon layer. Cells and species flagged by the check are verified by hand. Modern reinterpretation: island isolation is measured geodesically, not by Darwin's informal reckoning.

dataset.name: Data from: PHYLACINE 1.2: The Phylogenetic Atlas of Mammal Macroecology
dataset.publisher: Dryad (Faurby et al.; data paper in Ecology)
dataset.why_it_fits: It gives present natural geographic range maps (gridded rasters) for all ~5,800 mammal species, including recently extinct ones. It also gives trait data used for filtering: order, terrestrial/marine/freshwater flags and body mass. Ranges are modelled without human introductions, so native status is separated from introduced status. The test overlays each species' range cells on a land mask and measures distance to continents or great continental islands, then lists the species found beyond 483 km.
